concepts.concept: Controller finite-state (FSM) value that determines which outputs and actions the cache engine takes
concepts.writers: Reset assigns ctrl.state <= S_IDLE when rstn_i = '0' (lines 116-117); the synchronous process installs the next-state word on the clock edge with ctrl <= ctrl_nxt (line 126, guarded by rising_edge(clk_i)); ctrl_nxt.state is computed combinationally in ctrl_engine_comb (default at line 136 and explicit next-state assignments at lines 169, 175, 188, 192, 196, 200, 203, 211, 221, 231, 246, 254, 260, 265) driven by inputs such as host_req_i and bus_rsp_i.
concepts.observers: The FSM value determines externally visible outputs selected by the case at line 164: host_rsp_o assignments (host_rsp_o.ack at line 191, host_rsp_o <= bus_rsp_i at line 209, host_rsp_o.err at line 257), bus_req_o fields and strobe (default copy at line 159; addr/rw/lock/stb set at lines 227-231 and 238-240), and cache memory commands (cache_o.cmd_clr at line 219, cache_o.cmd_new at line 226, cache_o.data/we at lines 235-237) which produce externally observable memory effects.

confidentiality.reason: The FSM state is reflected on externally driven signals (for example host_rsp_o.ack asserted under S_LOOKUP at line 191), so an external observer can infer the controller state and the integrator may treat that state as secret.

integrity.reason: The register ctrl is updated unconditionally at the clock edge (ctrl <= ctrl_nxt at line 126) and ctrl_nxt is computed from untrusted external inputs (e.g. host_req_i inputs at lines 171-175 and bus_rsp_i inputs at lines 242-243), so outside inputs can change the FSM state while it controls behavior.

availability.reason: Several states wait for bus responses (e.g. S_DIRECT_RSP checks bus_rsp_i.ack at line 210), so an external bus that withholds acknowledgements can stall the FSM and prevent progress.

undermined behavior.reason: The FSM value is driven only by the clocked update ctrl <= ctrl_nxt (line 126) with next-state logic; there is no separate debug/test override that directly substitutes the FSM state.

concepts.concept: Host request inputs (address and request/privilege flags) that set which cache line / bus transaction is requested
concepts.writers: host_req_i is written by an external host (port declaration, line 37); the RTL reads and forwards fields into internal signals/outputs: cache_o.addr <= host_req_i.addr (line 149), cache_o.data <= host_req_i.data (line 151), bus_req_o <= host_req_i (line 159), and the combinational logic extracts tag/idx/ofs into ctrl_nxt.tag/idx/ofs at lines 180-182 and updates buf flags at lines 137-138.
concepts.observers: The host-provided request is forwarded to the external bus (bus_req_o <= host_req_i at line 159) and bus_req_o.addr is later driven in controller states (lines 227 and 238), so the requested address/flags are observable on the bus; host-visible responses (host_rsp_o at lines 154-156) also reflect request outcomes.

confidentiality.reason: Host request fields are forwarded to the external bus (bus_req_o <= host_req_i at line 159), so external parties can observe requested addresses/flags and the integrator may treat those inputs as secret.

integrity.reason: The request values originate from an external writer and are carried/forwarded by the RTL (bus_req_o <= host_req_i at line 159 and tag/idx derived at lines 180-181), so whether that writer is trusted depends on integration.

availability.reason: The controller combinationally ORs host_req_i.stb into the request buffer (ctrl_nxt.buf_req <= ctrl.buf_req or host_req_i.stb at line 137), so the RTL does not block acceptance of host requests.

undermined behavior.reason: host_req_i is driven by the external host (port at line 37) and the design contains no internal debug/test mechanism that replaces that input value.

concepts.concept: Bus request sent to the system bus (address, control bits, strobe) that the cache issues on misses or bypasses
concepts.writers: bus_req_o is driven by a default copy and by controller-state assignments: bus_req_o <= host_req_i (line 159); default/strobe/control fields are set to '0' at lines 160-161; bus_req_o.stb is asserted under control at lines 187,195,202,229; bus_req_o.fence <= '1' in S_CLEAR at line 217; bus_req_o.addr/rw/lock are driven from ctrl.tag/idx/ofs and constants in S_DOWNLOAD_REQ/S_DOWNLOAD_RSP at lines 225-231 and 235-240.
concepts.observers: bus_req_o is an output port (line 39) visible to the external bus; the RTL exposes its fields at the assignments and selections above (for example the default copy at line 159 and controller-driven addr/stb at lines 227-231 and 238-240).

confidentiality.reason: Bus requests are emitted on the module's external bus port (bus_req_o <= host_req_i at line 159), so addresses and control bits are observable outside the IP and may be sensitive.

integrity.reason: bus_req_o is driven both by a direct copy of host_req_i (line 159) and by controller-computed fields in different states (e.g. addr/stb/rw/lock in lines 227-231,238-240), so external inputs and state can change the outgoing bus request while it matters.

availability.reason: Request-response progression depends on external bus acknowledgements (bus_rsp_i.ack is checked at line 210 and 243), so the external bus can withhold ack and stall the request/response flow.

undermined behavior.reason: The controller's state selects alternate drivers for bus_req_o (default copy from host at line 159 versus controller-computed address/control in S_DOWNLOAD_REQ at line 227), so a state-selected mode substitutes a different source for the bus request.

concepts.concept: Cache-memory control commands and write-data that create/clear/invalidate cache lines and write fetched words into memory
concepts.writers: Controller combinational logic sets cache memory controls: defaults at lines 146-151 (cmd_* <= '0', cache_o.addr <= host_req_i.addr, cache_o.data <= host_req_i.data, cache_o.we <= (others => '0')); S_CLEAR asserts cache_o.cmd_clr <= '1' (line 219); S_DOWNLOAD_REQ sets cache_o.addr <= ctrl.tag & ctrl.idx & ctrl.ofs & "00" (line 225) and cache_o.cmd_new <= '1' (line 226); S_DOWNLOAD_RSP copies bus_rsp_i.data into cache_o.data (line 236) and asserts cache_o.we <= (others => '1') (line 237); S_LOOKUP drives cache_o.we <= host_req_i.ben for write-through on hits (line 194); S_DOWNLOAD_DONE may assert cache_o.cmd_inv <= '1' (line 255) when buf_err.
concepts.observers: These cache control signals are forwarded to the cache-memory instance (port map: clr_i <= cache_o.cmd_clr at line 283; inv_i <= cache_o.cmd_inv at line 284; new_i <= cache_o.cmd_new at line 285; addr_i <= cache_o.addr at line 288; we_i <= cache_o.we at line 289; wdata_i <= cache_o.data at line 290) and their effects are observable externally via host responses (host_rsp_o.data/ack/err at lines 154-156,191,256-257) after the memory updates.

confidentiality.reason: Cache control commands and write data are forwarded into the memory instance (clr_i/new_i/inv_i/addr_i/we_i/wdata_i mapped at lines 283-290), and the memory's contents and responses are observable to external masters (e.g. host_rsp_o at line 156), so these commands can be inferred externally.

integrity.reason: cache_o.data is driven directly from bus_rsp_i.data in S_DOWNLOAD_RSP (line 236) and cache_o.we is asserted (line 237), so an external bus supplying responses can control what is written into the cache memory.

availability.reason: The download sequence advances ofs and state only when bus_rsp_i.ack = '1' (checked at line 243), so an external bus that withholds acknowledgements can block memory updates and stall downloads.

undermined behavior.reason: The cache control commands are generated only by the controller state and bus responses (e.g. cache_o.cmd_new at line 226 and cache_o.data/we at lines 236-237); there is no separate debug/test override that directly substitutes these command sources.

concepts.concept: Cache hit indicator delivered by the on-chip cache memory (hit signal) that the controller reads to choose hit vs miss behavior
concepts.writers: The memory computes hit_o in neorv32_cache_memory (hit_o <= '1' when (valid_mem_rd = '1') and (tag_mem_rd = acc_tag) else '0' at line 405); that hit_o is connected to the top-level as neorv32_cache_memory_inst.hit_o => cache_i.sta_hit (port map line 286). The underlying storage (valid_mem/tag_mem) is updated in status_memory and tag_memory processes (valid_mem updates at lines 380-386, tag_mem write at line 397), which in turn are driven by clr_i/inv_i/new_i from the controller.
concepts.observers: The hit indicator is used by the controller and is visible indirectly to outsiders via responses: the controller gates immediate hit responses and host_rsp_o.ack (host_rsp_o.ack <= '1' on hit at line 191) and controls bus_req_o.stb behavior (lines 187,195,202), so hit status can be inferred by observing host responses and bus activity (not a direct port exposing 'hit').

confidentiality.reason: The hit result from the memory influences externally visible responses (host_rsp_o.ack asserted for hits at line 191), so an external observer can learn whether a given access hit the cache and the integrator may treat that as sensitive information.

integrity.reason: hit_o is computed inside the memory from valid_mem_rd and tag_mem_rd at line 405, and valid/tag bits are updated by clr_i/inv_i/new_i driven by the controller and bus responses (lines 380-386,397), so external inputs that influence those signals can change hit behavior while the controller depends on it.

availability.reason: valid_mem is cleared when clr_i = '1' (status_memory at line 380), and the controller can assert cache_o.cmd_clr (line 219) in response to fence requests, so external actions can force invalidation and prevent hits, affecting availability.

undermined behavior.reason: The hit indicator is computed by the memory's compare logic at line 405 and there is no separate debug/test input that force-writes or bypasses the hit signal directly.

concepts.concept: Read data returned from cache memory (rdata) that the module forwards to the host
concepts.writers: rdata_o is driven in the cache memory data process on the clock (rdata_o(7 downto 0) <= data_mem_b0(...), etc. at lines 425-428); the data arrays are written when we_i bits are asserted (data_mem_b0..b3 written at lines 413-423 from wdata_i); wdata_i is driven from cache_o.data (port map line 290) and cache_o.data is assigned from bus_rsp_i.data in S_DOWNLOAD_RSP (line 236) or from host_req_i.data by default (line 151). The top-level connects memory rdata_o to cache_i.data (port map line 291) and forwards it to the host (host_rsp_o.data <= cache_i.data at line 156).
concepts.observers: Host-visible read data is presented on host_rsp_o.data (line 156) and, in direct-response mode, the host may also receive bus responses forwarded by host_rsp_o <= bus_rsp_i (line 209); the memory's rdata path is visible externally via these host response outputs.

confidentiality.reason: Read data produced by the memory is forwarded to the external host (host_rsp_o.data <= cache_i.data at line 156), so externally observable outputs expose cached or fetched data and it may be sensitive.

integrity.reason: The memory bytes are written under we_i control (e.g. data_mem_b0 <= wdata_i(7 downto 0) when we_i(0) = '1' at line 413) and wdata_i can be supplied from bus responses (cache_o.data <= bus_rsp_i.data at line 236), so external writers can change what is later read out.

availability.reason: Block downloads and writes that populate the read data proceed only when bus_rsp_i.ack is asserted (line 243), so an external bus that withholds ack can stall availability of read data.

undermined behavior.reason: In S_DIRECT_RSP the controller forwards bus responses directly to the host (host_rsp_o <= bus_rsp_i at line 209), providing an alternate bypass path that replaces or bypasses cached rdata.

concepts.concept: Download error flag (buf_err) that causes invalidation and error reporting when a block download fails
concepts.writers: ctrl.buf_err is reset to '0' on rstn_i = '0' (line 120); the combinational default copies the stored flag (ctrl_nxt.buf_err <= ctrl.buf_err at line 139); S_LOOKUP clears the flag (ctrl_nxt.buf_err <= '0' at line 183); S_DOWNLOAD_RSP accumulates errors (ctrl_nxt.buf_err <= ctrl.buf_err or bus_rsp_i.err at line 242) which is then installed into ctrl on the clock (ctrl <= ctrl_nxt at line 126).
concepts.observers: The download error flag is surfaced to the host via host_rsp_o.err (host_rsp_o.err <= '1' when ctrl.buf_err = '1' in S_DOWNLOAD_DONE at line 257) and triggers cache invalidation (cache_o.cmd_inv <= '1' at line 255, mapped to memory inv_i at line 284), so the flag's presence and effects are externally observable.

confidentiality.reason: When a download has errors the flag causes host_rsp_o.err to be asserted (line 257), so external parties learn the error condition and the flag may be considered sensitive.

integrity.reason: The next-state buffer accumulates bus response errors (ctrl_nxt.buf_err <= ctrl.buf_err or bus_rsp_i.err at line 242) and that stored flag controls invalidation and error replies, so external bus error signals can set this flag.

availability.reason: The flag is explicitly cleared in normal lookup flow (ctrl_nxt.buf_err <= '0' at line 183) and its presence leads to a terminal handling path (S_DOWNLOAD_DONE), so the flag itself does not create an unbounded hang in the RTL.

undermined behavior.reason: buf_err is computed from bus response error bits and carried in the controller state (line 242); there is no separate debug/test override that substitutes a different source for this flag.
